It sounds like you're feeling a bit unsure how to read her messages—whether they're playful or coming from real anxiety about the friendship. That uncertainty can be tiring, especially when the checking-in happens often.

It might help to gently name what you're noticing. You could say something warm but honest, like: "I really enjoy being friends with you, and you don't have to worry about scaring me off. When you check in a lot, I sometimes can't tell if you're joking." That reassures her while also letting her know how the frequency feels to you. It's okay to have limits on how often you respond, too. A good friend will appreciate the honesty, and it gives her a chance to relax a little. You deserve friendships that feel comfortable for both of you.
